cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Yes of course, if you think I can help. What's it about?

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: It's my first media studies assignment, and I'm not sure how to go about it.

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: You must have done it last year.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Is that the one comparing the coverage of a particular story in a range of newspapers?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Well, there are several things.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: For example, there's the question of which page of the newspaper the item appears on.

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: You mean, because there's a big difference between having it on the front page and the

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: bottom of page ten, for instance?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Exactly. And that shows how important the editor thinks the story is.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Then there's the size – how many column inches the story is given, how many columns it

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: spreads over.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: It certainly does. It's all part of attracting the reader's attention.

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: What about graphics – whether there's anything visual in addition to the text?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Yes, you need to consider those, too, because they can have a big effect on the reader's

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: understanding of the story – sometimes a bigger effect than the text itself.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Then you'll need to look at how the item is put together: what structure is it given?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Bear in mind that not many people read beyond the first paragraph, so what has the

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: journalist put at the beginning?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: And if, say, three are conflicting opinions about something, does one appear near the

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: end, where people probably won't read it?

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: And newspapers sometimes give wrong or misleading information, don't they?

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: Either deliberately or by accident. Should I be looking at that, too?

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Yes, if you can.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Compare what's in different versions, and as far as possible, try and work out what's

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: true and what isn't.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: And that relates to a very important point: what's the writer's purpose, or at least the

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: most important one, if they have several.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: It may seem to be to inform the public, but often it's that they want to create fear, or

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: controversy, or to make somebody look ridiculous.

cues.speaker: EL
cues.text: Gosh, I see what you mean. And I suppose the writer may make assumptions about the reader.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: That's right – about their knowledge of the subject, their attitudes, and their level of

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: education, which means writing so that the readers understand without feeling patronised.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: All of that will make a difference to how story is presented.
